title: Coronation Chicken
subtitle: British curried chicken in a mango chutney and cream dressing
excerpt: Coronation chicken was created in 1953 for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II: cold poached chicken in a curried cream and mango chutney dressing. It became one of the most popular sandwich fillings in Britain and is now eaten at every occasion from sandwiches to picnics to buffets. The original recipe is simple and brilliant.
sourceNotes: Coronation chicken was created by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume for the banquet following the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II on 2 June 1953. They called it Poulet Reine Elizabeth. The dish uses a curried mayonnaise dressing that reflects the post-war British fascination with the foods of the Empire. It became one of the most widely eaten cold chicken dishes in Britain.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to 2 days ahead. Keeps well refrigerated.

content.text: The chicken can be poached or the recipe uses leftover roast chicken very well. The dressing should be made ahead and chilled -- it improves significantly over a few hours as the flavours meld. The apricot jam is not in the original recipe (which uses apricot puree) but is the closest substitute.

If using raw {{chicken-breast}} chicken: place in a pan with {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves, {{black-peppercorns}} peppercorns, and cold water to cover. Bring to a simmer and poach for 15 minutes until cooked through. Cool in the liquid. Drain, then cut or shred into large pieces.

Cook {{onion}} onion in {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add {{curry-powder}} curry powder and cook for 1 minute. Remove from the heat and cool. Mix with {{mayonnaise}} mayonnaise, {{double-cream}} whipped cream, {{mango-chutney}} mango chutney, {{tomato-puree}} tomato puree, {{lemon}} lemon juice, and {{salt-table}} salt.
Fold the chicken into the dressing. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Serve on a bed of lettuce, in sandwiches, or on jacket potatoes. Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over to finish.

items.symptom: The dressing is too thick and heavy
items.cause: The cream was not whipped or the mayonnaise was very thick.
items.fix: Fold in a tablespoon or two of cold water or a squeeze of lemon juice to loosen. The dressing should coat the chicken but not be solid.

content.text: Coronation chicken was created in 1953 by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume. They were tutors at a London cooking school. They served it at the banquet for the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II. The dish became one of the most famous British recipes of the 20th century. It now appears in sandwich shops, supermarkets, and home kitchens across Britain.
